correctness.rationale: The proof establishes terminality of out-/in-neighbor sets of non-singleton tournament subsets, at most one lost internal vertex, and recovery of all outside vertices on a direction change. Singleton terminal subsets are global sinks/sources and switch to all other vertices; a repeat of the same direction would violate the no-n-run induction. This yields at least n-r endpoints for all n>=2 and all allowed words, with equality in transitive tournaments. The clique-tight extension, rational run-series and 2n minimal DFA follow by explicit proofs. All 33,866 tournaments through order six were exhaustively checked by reachable product automata; finite tests are not universal proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full relevant text defines remanence and gives a chromatic constant-direction criterion, a bipartite characterization, and cyclic-orientation facts, but no sharp word-by-word count of reachable endpoints after arbitrarily many switches. The full K_n remanent-language corollary alone follows easily from the earlier acyclic-orientation observation and is not presented as the standalone novelty. The exact, sharp n-r subset bound and direction-change recovery are the scientific contribution; the complete graph-wide chi=omega and automata consequences contextualize it. Actual semantic research-record searches returned no equivalent result; unindexed prior work remains a risk.

value.rationale: The quantitative cardinality of feasible endpoints under arbitrary alternating orientation constraints is not captured by acceptance alone. The exact worst-case bound n-r and restoration of at least n-1 endpoints after every switch are natural sharp measures of nondeterministic path ambiguity. The result also yields a complete language classification and minimal automata for the broad chi=omega class (including perfect graphs). This is a structural theorem, not an arbitrary finite census or mere substitution, although the isolated complete-graph language corollary is elementary.
